title: People are triggers too
header_line: Jose's analysis of a book we are still naming. Not a summary of the book. Not affiliated with or endorsed by the author or publisher.

lines.text: Who do your habits become when you spend time with them?
Jose said that you can move to a bigger room, but what about relationships? How are business and friend relationships influencing your habits?
A student said: those are some of the fastest triggers back into any behavior, good or bad.
Jose asked: what kind of people do you attract? Are they open, curious, responsive? He recalled what parents say: you are who you hang around.

He said that this affects the clients you attract, the energy and the culture of the company. He gave examples of meetings where someone says: people in my circle told me I can trust you, and everything aligns.
A student said: successful people structure their environments. They are very conscious. They do not just say it is a bad environment with a lot of distractions.
A student said: the book talks about listing them out. Jose said: our mind is like post-it notes, and before you know it you have twenty or thirty of them stuck all over the place.
Write down the three people who most shape your habits. What does each one trigger?

exercise.title: Five minutes
steps: Write the three people you spend the most time with.
Write what each one triggers in you.
Write the people who trigger your best habits.
Write one relationship you could change or limit.
Write one new circle you want to join.

choices: They are some of the fastest triggers

check.q: What did Jose say about the people you attract?
What did a student say successful people do?

recap: People are triggers. Choose them. List your cues.
